lineage-traitorous-eight-names.claim: Eight Shockley Semiconductor engineers left to start their own company.
lineage-traitorous-eight-names.quote: The eight who left Shockley Semiconductor were Julius Blank, Victor Grinich, Jean Hoerni, Eugene Kleiner, Jay Last, Gordon Moore, Robert Noyce, and Sheldon Roberts.

lineage-fairchild-founded-1957.claim: The eight formed Fairchild Semiconductor on 18 September 1957 after agreeing terms with Sherman Fairchild in August.
lineage-fairchild-founded-1957.quote: In August 1957, they reached an agreement with Sherman Fairchild, and on September 18, 1957, they formed Fairchild Semiconductor.

lineage-fairchildren-1960.claim: By 1960 Fairchild was an incubator of Silicon Valley whose alumni created dozens of corporations, including Intel and AMD.
lineage-fairchildren-1960.quote: In 1960, it became an incubator of Silicon Valley and was directly or indirectly involved in the creation of dozens of corporations, including Intel and AMD.

lineage-fairchild-planar-1959.claim: Fairchild developed the planar process in 1959.
lineage-fairchild-planar-1959.quote: The planar process was developed at Fairchild Semiconductor in 1959 and it proved to be one of the most important single advances in semiconductor technology.

lineage-bell-passivation-preprint-1956.claim: Shockley circulated the Bell Labs passivation preprint to his senior staff, including Jean Hoerni, in December 1956.
lineage-bell-passivation-preprint-1956.quote: At Shockley Semiconductor, Shockley had circulated the preprint of their article in December 1956 to all his senior staff, including Jean Hoerni.

lineage-noyce-monolithic-ic-1959.claim: Robert Noyce invented the first monolithic integrated circuit in 1959.
lineage-noyce-monolithic-ic-1959.quote: Robert Noyce invented the first monolithic integrated circuit in 1959.

lineage-kilby-nobel-2000.claim: Jack Kilby won the 2000 Nobel Prize in physics for his part in the invention of the integrated circuit.
lineage-kilby-nobel-2000.quote: Kilby won the 2000 Nobel Prize in physics for his part in the invention of the integrated circuit.

lineage-fairchild-first-batch-ibm.claim: Fairchild's first batch of 100 devices was sold to IBM at $150 apiece for the B-70 bomber's computer.
lineage-fairchild-first-batch-ibm.quote: The first batch of 100 was sold to IBM for $150 apiece in order to build the computer for the B-70 bomber.

lineage-intel-founded-1968.claim: Intel was founded in 1968 by Gordon Moore and Robert Noyce with investor Arthur Rock.
lineage-intel-founded-1968.quote: Intel was founded in 1968 by engineers Gordon Moore and Robert Noyce, along with investor Arthur Rock, and is associated with the executive leadership and vision of Andrew Grove.

lineage-faggin-left-fairchild-1970.claim: Federico Faggin left Fairchild for Intel in 1970 to design the first microprocessors.
lineage-faggin-left-fairchild-1970.quote: Federico Faggin, frustrated, left Fairchild to join Intel in 1970 and design the first microprocessors using SGT.

lineage-intel-1103-dram-1970.claim: Intel's 1103, released in 1970, was the first commercially available DRAM.
lineage-intel-1103-dram-1970.quote: The three-transistor cell implemented in the first commercially available dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), the 1103 released in 1970, solved these issues.

lineage-intel-1103-bestseller-1972.claim: The 1103 was the world's bestselling semiconductor memory chip by 1972.
lineage-intel-1103-bestseller-1972.quote: The 1103 was the bestselling semiconductor memory chip in the world by 1972, as it replaced core memory in many applications.

lineage-intel-4004-1971.claim: Intel introduced the 4004 microprocessor in 1971, built for Busicom, but it did not become Intel's core business until the mid-1980s.
lineage-intel-4004-1971.quote: Originally developed for the Japanese company Busicom to replace a number of ASICs in a calculator already produced by Busicom, the Intel 4004 was introduced to the mass market on November 15, 1971, though the microprocessor did not become the core of Intel's business until the mid-1980s.

lineage-intel-japan-dram-1983.claim: In 1983 Japanese memory makers squeezed Intel's profits and Andy Grove refocused Intel on microprocessors.
lineage-intel-japan-dram-1983.quote: In 1983, at the dawn of the personal computer era, Intel's profits came under increased pressure from Japanese memory-chip manufacturers, and then-president Andy Grove focused the company on microprocessors.

lineage-ibm-pc-8088-1981.claim: The IBM PC, released 12 August 1981, used an Intel 8088 processor.
lineage-ibm-pc-8088-1981.quote: Powered by an x86-architecture Intel 8088 processor, the machine was based on open architecture and third-party peripherals.

lineage-compaq-386-1986.claim: Compaq, the first IBM PC clone maker, shipped the first 80386-based system in 1986, beating IBM and making Intel a key component supplier.
lineage-compaq-386-1986.quote: Compaq, the first IBM PC "clone" manufacturer, produced a desktop system based on the faster 80286 processor in 1985 and in 1986 quickly followed with the first 80386-based system, beating IBM and establishing a competitive market for PC-compatible systems and setting up Intel as a key component supplier.

lineage-tsmc-founded-1987.claim: TSMC was established in 1987 as a joint venture of Taiwan's government, ITRI and private investors, and became the world's first dedicated foundry.
lineage-tsmc-founded-1987.quote: TSMC was established in 1987 as a joint venture between Taiwan's government, the Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI), and private investors.

lineage-tsmc-foundry-share-2026.claim: TSMC holds approximately 70% of the global foundry market.
lineage-tsmc-foundry-share-2026.quote: It holds a commanding majority in the semiconductor foundry market, accounting for approximately 70% of the global market share.

lineage-tsmc-first-euv-volume.claim: TSMC was the first foundry to commercialise ASML's EUV lithography in high volume.
lineage-tsmc-first-euv-volume.quote: TSMC was the first foundry to market 7-nanometre and 5-nanometre (used by the 2020 Apple A14 and M1 SoCs, the MediaTek Dimensity 8100, and AMD Ryzen 7000 series processors) production capabilities, and the first to commercialise ASML's extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography technology in high volume.

lineage-nvidia-founded-1993.claim: Nvidia was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem.
lineage-nvidia-founded-1993.quote: Founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem, Nvidia has been described as a Big Tech company and is among the largest companies by market capitalization.

lineage-sega-invest-5m.claim: Sega's Shoichiro Irimajiri persuaded Sega to invest $5 million in Nvidia after Nvidia had failed to deliver on its contract.
lineage-sega-invest-5m.quote: However, Irimajiri believed in Nvidia's potential and persuaded Sega's management to invest $5 million into the company.

lineage-sega-sold-15m.claim: Sega sold its Nvidia stock for $15 million after 2000.
lineage-sega-sold-15m.quote: After Irimajiri left Sega in 2000, Sega sold its Nvidia stock for $15 million.

lineage-geforce-256-1999.claim: In late 1999 Nvidia released the GeForce 256, its first product marketed as a GPU.
lineage-geforce-256-1999.quote: In late 1999, Nvidia released the GeForce 256 (NV10), its first product expressly marketed as a GPU, which was most notable for introducing onboard transformation and lighting (T&L) to consumer-level 3D hardware.

lineage-nvidia-acquires-3dfx-2000.claim: In December 2000 Nvidia agreed to acquire the intellectual assets of its one-time rival 3dfx.
lineage-nvidia-acquires-3dfx-2000.quote: In December 2000, Nvidia reached an agreement to acquire the intellectual assets of its one-time rival 3dfx, a pioneer in consumer 3D graphics technology leading the field from the mid-1990s until 2000.

lineage-cuda-released-2007.claim: CUDA was created in 2004 and officially released in 2007.
lineage-cuda-released-2007.quote: CUDA was created in 2004 and was officially released in 2007.

lineage-alexnet-two-gtx580-2012.claim: AlexNet was trained for five to six days on two Nvidia GTX 580 GPUs and won the 2012 ImageNet competition.
lineage-alexnet-two-gtx580-2012.quote: The model was trained for 90 epochs over a period of five to six days using two Nvidia GTX 580 GPUs (3GB each).

lineage-gtx580-price-500.claim: Each GTX 580 was priced at US$500 on release.
lineage-gtx580-price-500.quote: These GPUs have a theoretical performance of 1.581 TFLOPS in float32 and were priced at US$500 upon release.

lineage-dgx1-openai-2016.claim: Nvidia gifted its first DGX-1 to OpenAI in August 2016, cutting a training run from six days to two hours.
lineage-dgx1-openai-2016.quote: Nvidia gifted its first DGX-1 to OpenAI in August 2016 to help it train larger and more complex AI models with the capability of reducing processing time from six days to two hours.

lineage-mellanox-6-9bn-2019.claim: Nvidia announced on 11 March 2019 that it would acquire Mellanox for $6.9 billion.
lineage-mellanox-6-9bn-2019.quote: On March 11, 2019, Nvidia announced its intent to acquire the company for $6.9 billion.

lineage-attention-transformer-2017.claim: The Transformer, based solely on attention, was submitted to arXiv on 12 June 2017.
lineage-attention-transformer-2017.quote: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

lineage-attention-bleu-8gpu.claim: The Transformer reached 41.8 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-French after 3.5 days on eight GPUs.
lineage-attention-bleu-8gpu.quote: On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature.

lineage-transformer-google-2017.claim: The original transformer architecture was proposed in the 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need' by researchers at Google.
lineage-transformer-google-2017.quote: The original version of the transformer architecture was proposed in the 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" by researchers at Google.

lineage-scaling-laws-2020.claim: Kaplan et al. found language-model loss scales as a power law in model size, data and compute over more than seven orders of magnitude (submitted 23 January 2020).
lineage-scaling-laws-2020.quote: The loss scales as a power-law with model size, dataset size, and the amount of compute used for training, with some trends spanning more than seven orders of magnitude.

lineage-gpt3-175b-2020.claim: GPT-3 had 175 billion parameters, ten times any previous non-sparse language model (submitted 28 May 2020).
lineage-gpt3-175b-2020.quote: Specifically, we train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, 10x more than any previous non-sparse language model, and test its performance in the few-shot setting.

lineage-anthropic-founders-from-openai.claim: Eleven OpenAI employees left between December 2020 and January 2021 to establish Anthropic.
lineage-anthropic-founders-from-openai.quote: Eleven employees left OpenAI, mostly between December 2020 and January 2021, in order to establish Anthropic.

lineage-chatgpt-release-2022.quote: Originally released on November 30, 2022, the product uses large language models – specifically generative pre-trained transformers (GPTs) – to generate text, speech, and images in response to user prompts.

lineage-chatgpt-users-2026.claim: ChatGPT reached 100 million monthly users two months after release and 900 million weekly users in February 2026.
lineage-chatgpt-users-2026.quote: ChatGPT was quickly adopted, reaching 100 million monthly active users two months after its release and 900 million weekly active users in February 2026.

lineage-asml-euv-1997.claim: ASML began developing EUV lithography in 1997.
lineage-asml-euv-1997.quote: Meanwhile, in 1997, ASML began developing its EUV lithography technology.

lineage-asml-coinvest-2012.claim: In 2012 ASML sold 23 percent of itself to Intel, TSMC and Samsung.
lineage-asml-coinvest-2012.quote: To achieve this, ASML launched a co-investment program in 2012, under which 23 percent of the company was sold to its three largest customers: Intel, TSMC and Samsung.

lineage-intel-asml-4-1bn-2012.claim: Intel invested $4.1 billion in ASML in July 2012 for a 15 percent stake.
lineage-intel-asml-4-1bn-2012.quote: To help fund the expensive research and development required, Intel invested $4.1 billion in ASML in July 2012 in exchange for a 15 percent stake.

lineage-asml-only-euv-2026.claim: ASML is, as of 2026, the world's only manufacturer of EUV lithography machines.
lineage-asml-only-euv-2026.quote: It is the largest supplier to the semiconductor industry and, as of 2026[update] , the world's only manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which are required to manufacture the most advanced semiconductor chips.

lineage-nvidia-2tn-180-days.claim: Nvidia took 180 days to go from $1 trillion to $2 trillion; Apple and Microsoft each took over 500.
lineage-nvidia-2tn-180-days.quote: Nvidia needed only 180 days to get to $2 trillion from $1 trillion, while the first two companies, Apple and Microsoft, each took over 500 days.

lineage-nvidia-5tn-2025.claim: On 29 October 2025 Nvidia became the first company to reach a $5 trillion market capitalization.
lineage-nvidia-5tn-2025.quote: On October 29, 2025, Nvidia became the first company to reach a market capitalization of $5 trillion.

lineage-nvidia-marketcap-now.claim: NVIDIA's market capitalization in November 2026 was $4.506 trillion, the world's 2nd most valuable company by that data.
lineage-nvidia-marketcap-now.quote: Market capitalization of NVIDIA (NVDA) Market cap: $4.506 Trillion USD As of November 2026

lineage-nvidia-gpu-share-2025.claim: As of Q1 2025 Nvidia held 92% of the discrete desktop and laptop GPU market.
lineage-nvidia-gpu-share-2025.period: Q1 2025 (market: discrete desktop and laptop GPUs, not AI accelerators)
lineage-nvidia-gpu-share-2025.quote: As of the first quarter of 2025, Nvidia held a 92% share of the discrete desktop and laptop GPU market.

lineage-us-gov-intel-stake-2025.claim: In August 2025 the US government bought 433.3 million Intel shares at $20.47, a 9.9% stake.
lineage-us-gov-intel-stake-2025.quote: In August 2025, the United States government purchased 433.3 million Intel shares at $20.47 per share, equivalent to a 9.9% stake.

lineage-hutter-compression-ai.claim: The Hutter Prize, launched in 2006, rests on the organizers' belief that text compression and AI are equivalent problems.
lineage-hutter-compression-ai.quote: Launched in 2006, the prize awards 5,000 euros for each one percent improvement

lineage-huang-amd-first-job.claim: Jensen Huang began as a microchip designer in Silicon Valley and chose AMD over Texas Instruments and LSI Logic.
lineage-huang-amd-first-job.quote: He was approached for positions at Texas Instruments, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and LSI Logic,[30] ultimately choosing the California-based AMD due to already being familiar with the company.

century-standard-oil-1904-share.claim: In 1904 Standard Oil controlled 91% of US oil refining and 85% of final sales.
century-standard-oil-1904-share.quote: In 1904 Standard Oil controlled 91% of oil refinement and 85% of final sales in the United States.[31]

century-standard-oil-1911-share.claim: Standard Oil's market share had fallen to 64% by 1911, when it was ordered broken up.
century-standard-oil-1911-share.quote: Standard's market share was 64% by 1911 when Standard was ordered broken up.[50]

century-us-steel-1901-share.claim: In 1901 U.S. Steel produced roughly two-thirds of the steel made in the United States.
century-us-steel-1901-share.quote: In 1901, the company was far and away the largest steel manufacturer, producing roughly two-thirds of the steel in the United States.[20]

century-ibm-1960s-share.claim: In the 1960s and 1970s IBM produced 80 percent of computers in the US and 70 percent worldwide.
century-ibm-1960s-share.quote: During the 1960s and 1970s, the IBM mainframe, exemplified by the System/360 and its successors, was the world's dominant computing platform, with the company producing 80 percent of computers in the U.S. and 70 percent of computers worldwide.[11]

century-ibm-1993-loss.claim: In 1993 IBM posted an $8 billion loss, the biggest in American corporate history at the time.
century-ibm-1993-loss.quote: In 1993, IBM posted an $8 billion loss – at the time the biggest in American corporate history.[61]

century-gm-lost-title-2008.claim: GM was the world's largest automaker for 77 years before losing the title to Toyota in 2008.
century-gm-lost-title-2008.quote: By total sales, it has continuously been the largest automaker in the United States, and was the largest in the world for 77 years before losing the title to Toyota in 2008.[4][5]

century-ge-2000-market-cap.claim: In August 2000 General Electric had a market capitalization of $601 billion and was the most valuable company in the world.
century-ge-2000-market-cap.quote: In August 2000, the company had a market capitalization of $601 billion, and was the most valuable company in the world.[176]

century-ge-removed-dow-2018.claim: GE was removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average on 28 June 2018 after its weight fell below 1% of the index.
century-ge-removed-dow-2018.quote: GE was removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average on June 28, 2018, after the value had dropped below 1% of the index's weight.[206]

century-nokia-2007-share.claim: In Q4 2007 Nokia reached an all-time high 40.4% of handset sales and 51% of smartphones.
century-nokia-2007-share.quote: However, by 2006, the company was steadily gaining again[74][75] and in Q4 2007 reached its all-time high figure of 40.4%.[76]

century-blackberry-subscribers.claim: BlackBerry had 85 million subscribers at its September 2011 peak, down to 23 million by March 2016.
century-blackberry-subscribers.quote: At its peak in September 2011, there were 85 million BlackBerry services subscribers worldwide;[21][22] its numbers had fallen to 23 million in March 2016 as its remaining international strongholds also lost share.

century-blockbuster-2004-peak.claim: At its 2004 peak Blockbuster employed 84,300 people and operated 9,094 stores.
century-blockbuster-2004-peak.quote: At its peak in 2004,[4][5] Blockbuster employed 84,300 people worldwide and operated 9,094 stores.[6]

century-blockbuster-declined-netflix.claim: In 2000 Blockbuster turned down a chance to buy Netflix for $50 million.
century-blockbuster-declined-netflix.quote: Also in 2000, Blockbuster turned down a chance to purchase the fledgling Netflix for $50 million (~$88.7 million in 2025).[57]

century-blockbuster-2010-bankruptcy.claim: On 23 September 2010 Blockbuster filed for Chapter 11 with $900 million of debt, citing competition from Netflix, Redbox and video on demand.
century-blockbuster-2010-bankruptcy.quote: On September 23, 2010, Blockbuster filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection due to challenging losses, $900 million (~$1.3 billion in 2025) in debt, and strong competition from Netflix, Redbox, and video on-demand services.[82][83]

century-fuji-kodak-share.claim: Fuji's share of the US film market rose from 10% in the early 1990s to 17% in 1997, taking share from Kodak.
century-fuji-kodak-share.quote: Fuji opened a film plant in the U.S., and its aggressive marketing and price cutting began taking market share from Kodak, rising from a 10% share in the early 1990s to 17% in 1997.[12]

century-kodak-2012-chapter11.claim: Kodak filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in January 2012.
century-kodak-2012-chapter11.quote: These strategies failed to improve the company's finances, and in January 2012, Kodak filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York.[16][17][18]

century-walmart-passes-sears.claim: Walmart became the largest US retailer by revenue by October 1989.
century-walmart-passes-sears.quote: By 1988, it was the most profitable retailer in the U.S.,[27] and it had become the largest in terms of revenue by October 1989.[28]

century-enron-2000-revenue.claim: Enron claimed revenues of nearly $101 billion in 2000 and went bankrupt on 2 December 2001.
century-enron-2000-revenue.quote: Before its bankruptcy on December 2, 2001, Enron employed approximately 20,600 staff and was a major electricity, natural gas, communications, and pulp and paper company, with claimed revenues of nearly $101 billion during 2000.[1]

century-lehman-assets.claim: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy on 15 September 2008 with assets worth $639 billion.
century-lehman-assets.quote: Shortly before 1 am Monday morning (UTC−5), Lehman Brothers Holdings announced it would file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection citing bank debt of $613 billion, $155 billion in bond debt,[109] and assets worth $639 billion.[110]

century-nikkei-1989-peak.claim: The Nikkei 225 touched a record 38,957.44 on 29 December 1989 and had halved by August 1990.
century-nikkei-1989-peak.quote: Nikkei 225 touched a then-historical all-time high of 38,957.44 on December 29, 1989.[12]

century-yahoo-google-offer.claim: In 1998 Yahoo declined to buy Google for $1 million, and in 2002 its final offer of $3 billion was rejected.
century-yahoo-google-offer.quote: The company had two failed attempts to acquire Google; in 1998, Larry Page and Sergey Brin approached Yahoo to sell their nascent search engine for $1 million, but Yahoo declined the offer.[33][34]

century-microsoft-yahoo-bid.claim: In February 2008 Microsoft made an unsolicited $44.6 billion bid for Yahoo, which Yahoo's board resisted.
century-microsoft-yahoo-bid.quote: In February 2008, Microsoft made an unsolicited bid to acquire Yahoo for $44.6 billion.[36][37]

century-instagram-acquired.claim: In April 2012 Facebook acquired Instagram for approximately US$1 billion in cash and stock.
century-instagram-acquired.quote: In April 2012, Facebook acquired the service for approximately US$1 billion in cash and stock.

century-aws-share-2023.claim: As of Q1 2023 AWS had 31% of cloud infrastructure, against Azure 25% and Google Cloud 11%.
century-aws-share-2023.quote: As of 2023 Q1, AWS has 31% market share for cloud infrastructure while the next two competitors Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud have 25%, and 11% respectively, according to Synergy Research Group.[12][13]

century-xerox-parc-apple-1979.claim: In 1979 Steve Jobs arranged a visit to Xerox PARC where Apple saw the Alto's technology, in exchange for Xerox buying Apple stock options.
century-xerox-parc-apple-1979.quote: In 1979, Steve Jobs arranged a visit to Xerox PARC, during which Apple Computer personnel received demonstrations of Xerox technology in exchange for Xerox being able to purchase stock options in Apple.[9]

century-microsoft-guilty-2000.claim: On 3 April 2000 Judge Jackson ruled that Microsoft was guilty of monopolization and tying under the Sherman Act.
century-microsoft-guilty-2000.quote: Tangentially to all of speculation, on April 3, 2000 Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson issued his conclusions of law in the case of United States v. Microsoft Corp. (2001) and ruled that Microsoft was guilty of monopolization and tying in violation of the Sherman Antitrust Act.

century-huawei-passes-ericsson.claim: In 2012 Huawei surpassed Ericsson to become the world's largest telecommunications equipment manufacturer.
century-huawei-passes-ericsson.quote: In 2012, it surpassed Ericsson to become the world's largest telecommunications equipment manufacturer.[6]

century-ford-assembly-line-1913.claim: Ford introduced the first moving assembly line in 1913 at its Highland Park factory.
century-ford-assembly-line-1913.quote: More efficient production methods were needed to make automobiles affordable for middle class people; Ford contributed to this effort through a variety of innovations, including the introduction of the first moving assembly line in 1913 at the Ford factory in Highland Park.[18]

century-bell-breakup.claim: The Bell System consisted of AT&T plus 24 local Bell Operating Companies and Western Electric, which made almost all of its equipment.
century-bell-breakup.quote: It consisted of the parent American Telephone & Telegraph Company (AT&T), which directly provided long-distance service, while local service was provided by 24 local Bell Operating Companies, which were owned whole or in part by AT&T, while its manufacturing subsidiary Western Electric produced almost all of its equipment, which was largely designed at the research and development subsidiary Bell Labs.

century-apple-1t-2018.claim: On 2 August 2018 Apple became the first publicly traded US company to reach a $1 trillion market value.
century-apple-1t-2018.quote: On August 2, 2018, Apple became the first publicly traded US company to reach a $1 trillion market value,[284][285] and, as of October 2025[update] , is valued at just over $4 trillion.[286]

century-walmart-2026-rank.claim: As of 2026 Walmart is the second-largest company by revenue globally and the world's largest private employer, with 2.1 million employees.
century-walmart-2026-rank.quote: As of 2026, Walmart is the second-largest company by revenue globally[f] and the largest private employer in the world,[g] with 2.1 million employees.[a]

century-sears-bankruptcy-2018.claim: Sears Holdings filed for Chapter 11 on 15 October 2018 and sold its assets to ESL Investments in 2019.
century-sears-bankruptcy-2018.quote: It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on October 15, 2018, and sold its assets to ESL Investments in 2019.[9]

century-gm-bailout-2009.claim: By March 2009 GM had received $17.4 billion in bailouts when the US President forced the resignation of its CEO.
century-gm-bailout-2009.quote: In March 2009, after the company had received $17.4 billion in bailouts but was not effective in a turnaround, President Barack Obama forced the resignation of CEO Rick Wagoner.[113]

century-nokia-windows-phone-2011.claim: On 11 February 2011 Nokia announced a partnership with Microsoft to adopt Windows Phone 7 as its primary smartphone operating system.
century-nokia-windows-phone-2011.quote: On 11 February 2011, Nokia announced a "strategic partnership" with Microsoft, under which it would adopt Windows Phone 7 as its primary operating system on smartphones, and integrate its services and platforms with its own, including Bing as its default search engine, and integration of Nokia Maps data into Bing Maps.

century-msdos-90pct.claim: Of 15 million Americans who used a personal computer at work, more than 90% used MS-DOS.
century-msdos-90pct.quote: Of the 15 million Americans who used a personal computer in their job, more than 90% used MS-DOS.[5]

century-microsoft-breakup-ordered-2000.claim: On 7 June 2000 the District Court ordered a breakup of Microsoft as its remedy.
century-microsoft-breakup-ordered-2000.quote: On June 7, 2000, the District Court ordered a breakup of Microsoft as its remedy.[22]

century-bell-divestiture-1984.claim: The divestiture of the local operating companies to the Baby Bells became effective on 1 January 1984.
century-bell-divestiture-1984.quote: The divesture of the local operating companies to the Baby Bells became effective on January 1, 1984.

century-yahoo-verizon-2016.claim: On 25 July 2016 Verizon announced it would buy Yahoo's core Internet business for $4.83 billion.
century-yahoo-verizon-2016.quote: On July 25, 2016, Verizon Communications announced it would acquire Yahoo's core Internet business for $4.83 billion, a stunning collapse from the company's peak valuation.[97][98][99][100]

century-china-manufacturing-nine.claim: China is the world's largest manufacturing economy; its production exceeds that of the nine next largest manufacturers combined.
century-china-manufacturing-nine.quote: China is the world's largest manufacturing industrial economy and exporter of goods.

century-toyota-2024-largest.claim: As of 2024 Toyota was the world's largest car company with revenues exceeding US$400 billion.
century-toyota-2024-largest.quote: As of 2024[update] , Toyota was the world's largest car company with revenues exceeding US$400 billion.

century-whatsapp-2014.claim: In February 2014 Facebook agreed to acquire WhatsApp for US$19 billion, its largest acquisition to date.
century-whatsapp-2014.quote: Feb 19, 2014 Facebook, Inc. announces its acquisition of WhatsApp for US$19 billion, its largest acquisition to date.[43]

century-google-search-share-2026.claim: In October 2026 Google held 91.05% of worldwide search, Bing 4.8% and Yahoo! 1.18%.
century-google-search-share-2026.quote: Search Engine Market Share Worldwide - October 2026 Google 91.05% bing 4.8% Yahoo! 1.18% YANDEX 1.14% DuckDuckGo 0.64% Baidu 0.42%

century-mobile-os-share-2026.claim: In October 2026 Android held 72.36% and iOS 27.61% of worldwide mobile operating systems; Windows 0%.
century-mobile-os-share-2026.quote: Mobile Operating System Market Share Worldwide - October 2026 Android 72.36% iOS 27.61% Linux 0.01% KaiOS 0.01% Windows 0% Samsung 0%

archetypes-mongol-horses-per-soldier.claim: Each Mongol soldier typically maintained three or four horses, rotating mounts to keep up speed for days.
archetypes-mongol-horses-per-soldier.unit: horses per soldier (upper figure; sources say three or four)
archetypes-mongol-horses-per-soldier.quote: Each Mongol soldier typically maintained three or four horses.

archetypes-mongol-empire-extent.claim: By Genghis Khan's death in 1227 the Mongol Empire ruled from the Pacific to the Caspian, twice the size of the Roman Empire, the largest contiguous state in history.
archetypes-mongol-empire-extent.quote: Genghis Khan died on 18 August 1227, by which time the Mongol Empire ruled from the Pacific Ocean to the Caspian Sea, twice the size of the Roman Empire or Umayyad Caliphate at their height, and the largest contiguous state in history.

archetypes-stirrup-chinese-origin.claim: The stirrup was invented in China in the 4th century and spread across Eurasia through nomadic peoples; it was not a Mongol invention.
archetypes-stirrup-chinese-origin.quote: The stirrup was invented in the Chinese Jin dynasty during the 4th century, was in common use throughout China by the 5th century, and was spread across Eurasia to Europe through the nomadic peoples of Central Eurasia by the 7th or 8th century.

archetypes-mongol-bow-quivers.claim: Mongol cavalry carried quivers of 60 arrows, strapped to riders and to their horses, and two or three bows each.
archetypes-mongol-bow-quivers.quote: Quivers containing 60 arrows were strapped to the backs of their cavalrymen and to their horses.

archetypes-mongol-meritocracy.claim: Genghis Khan turned the Mongols' tribal structure into an integrated meritocracy serving the ruling family.
archetypes-mongol-meritocracy.quote: Carrying out reforms designed to ensure long-term stability, he transformed the Mongols' tribal structure into an integrated meritocracy dedicated to the service of the ruling family.

archetypes-mongol-prisoners-driven-forwa.claim: The Mongols gathered prisoners captured in earlier battles and drove them forward in sieges and battles.
archetypes-mongol-prisoners-driven-forwa.quote: The Mongols would gather prisoners captured in previous battles and would drive them forward in sieges and battles.

archetypes-napoleon-emperor-1804.claim: On 18 May 1804 the Senate vested the government of the French Republic in an emperor, Napoleon.
archetypes-napoleon-emperor-1804.quote: On May 18, 1804, the Sénat conservateur vested the Republican government of the French First Republic in an emperor, and preparations for the coronation followed.

archetypes-napoleon-crowned-himself.claim: Napoleon decided to crown himself, so the coronation omitted the formula that showed a monarch receiving his crown from the Church.
archetypes-napoleon-crowned-himself.quote: As for the omitted Roman formula Accipe coronam..., which depicted the monarch as receiving his crown from the Church, its use would have clashed with Napoleon's decision to crown himself.

archetypes-napoleon-levy-1793.claim: In February 1793 the French National Convention decreed a national levy of about 300,000 men, a step toward the levee en masse.
archetypes-napoleon-levy-1793.quote: This ragtag group was spread thin, and, by February 1793, the new regime needed more men, so the National Convention passed a decree on 24 February allowing for the national levy of about 300,000 with each French département to supply a quota of recruits.

archetypes-napoleon-grande-armee-corps.claim: The Grande Armée consisted, on formation, of six corps led by Napoleon's marshals and senior generals.
archetypes-napoleon-grande-armee-corps.quote: Upon its formation, it consisted of six corps led by Napoleon's marshals and senior generals.

archetypes-napoleon-massed-artillery.claim: After 1807 Napoleon used massed artillery as a spearhead to pound a break in the enemy's line.
archetypes-napoleon-massed-artillery.quote: Napoleon, rather than relying on infantry to wear away the enemy's defences, could now use massed artillery as a spearhead to pound a break in the enemy's line.

archetypes-napoleon-leipzig-1813.claim: The Sixth Coalition defeated Napoleon at Leipzig in October 1813.
archetypes-napoleon-leipzig-1813.quote: The Sixth Coalition defeated Napoleon at Leipzig in October 1813.

archetypes-napoleon-waterloo-1815.claim: The Seventh Coalition defeated Napoleon at Waterloo in June 1815 and exiled him to Saint Helena.
archetypes-napoleon-waterloo-1815.quote: The allies formed the Seventh Coalition, which defeated him at Waterloo in June 1815 and exiled him to the British island of Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.

archetypes-vienna-congress-dates.claim: The Congress of Vienna, chaired by Metternich, was held from September 1814 to June 1815.
archetypes-vienna-congress-dates.quote: The Congress was chaired by Austrian statesman Klemens von Metternich (Duke Metternich)  and was held in Vienna from September 1814 to June 1815.

archetypes-vienna-concert-of-europe.claim: The Vienna settlement gave birth to the Concert of Europe, which maintained the balance of powers until the First World War in 1914.
archetypes-vienna-concert-of-europe.quote: The Congress of Vienna settlement gave birth to the Concert of Europe, an international political doctrine that emphasized the maintaining of political boundaries, the balance of powers, and respecting spheres of influence and which guided foreign policy among the nations of Europe until the outbreak of the First World War in 1914.

archetypes-alexander-phalanx-edge.claim: Alexander's phalanx, armed with long pikes, had a considerable advantage over the Persians' scimitars and javelins.
archetypes-alexander-phalanx-edge.quote: This ensured that Alexander would not be outflanked, while his phalanx, armed with long pikes, had a considerable advantage over the Persians' scimitars and javelins.

archetypes-gaugamela-wedge.claim: At Gaugamela Alexander drew the Persian cavalry to the flanks to open a gap, then led a wedge into the weakened centre.
archetypes-gaugamela-wedge.quote: He formed his units into a giant wedge, with him leading the charge.

archetypes-alexander-persian-officers.claim: Alexander gave Persians command posts and Macedonian military titles to Persian units, which his Macedonians resented.
archetypes-alexander-persian-officers.quote: After three days, unable to persuade his men to back down, Alexander gave Persians command posts in the army and conferred Macedonian military titles upon Persian units.

archetypes-darius-immortals.claim: Darius's only respectable infantry were 2,000 Greek hoplites and his 10,000 Immortals.
archetypes-darius-immortals.quote: The only respectable infantry Darius had were his 2,000 Greek hoplites[7] and his personal bodyguard, the 10,000 Immortals.

archetypes-trophic-ten-percent.claim: Only about 10% of the energy passing between trophic levels is converted to biomass, which limits the number of levels.
archetypes-trophic-ten-percent.quote: Only about 10% of the energy transferred between each trophic level is converted to biomass.

archetypes-kpg-three-quarters.claim: The end-Cretaceous extinction killed three-quarters (75%) of plant and animal species.
archetypes-kpg-three-quarters.quote: Based on marine fossils, it is estimated that 75% or more of all species became extinct.

archetypes-kpg-mammals-survived.claim: All major Late Cretaceous mammalian lineages survived the end-Cretaceous extinction, although they suffered losses.
archetypes-kpg-mammals-survived.quote: All major Late Cretaceous mammalian lineages, including monotremes (egg-laying mammals), multituberculates, metatherians (which includes modern marsupials), eutherians (which includes modern placentals), meridiolestidans,[150] and gondwanatheres[151] survived the K–Pg extinction event, although they suffered losses.

archetypes-kpg-dinosaurs-no-shelter.claim: There is no evidence that late Maastrichtian non-avian dinosaurs could burrow, swim or dive, so they could not shelter from the worst of the stress.
archetypes-kpg-dinosaurs-no-shelter.quote: There is no evidence that late Maastrichtian non-avian dinosaurs could burrow, swim, or dive, which suggests they were unable to shelter themselves from the worst parts of any environmental stress that occurred at the K–Pg boundary.

archetypes-convergent-flight.claim: Flying insects, birds, pterosaurs and bats independently evolved flight, a classic case of convergent evolution.
archetypes-convergent-flight.quote: The recurrent evolution of flight is a classic example, as flying insects, birds, pterosaurs, and bats have independently evolved the useful capacity of flight.

archetypes-lotka-volterra.claim: The Lotka-Volterra equations describe two species interacting, one as predator and one as prey.
archetypes-lotka-volterra.quote: The Lotka–Volterra equations, also known as the Lotka–Volterra predator–prey model, are a pair of first-order nonlinear differential equations, frequently used to describe the dynamics of biological systems in which two species interact, one as a predator and the other as prey.

archetypes-bretton-woods-44.claim: The Bretton Woods system set the rules of commercial relations among 44 countries after the 1944 agreement until 1976.
archetypes-bretton-woods-44.quote: The Bretton Woods system of monetary management established the rules for commercial relations[1] among 44 countries, including the United Kingdom, United States, Canada, European countries, and Australia, after the 1944 Bretton Woods Agreement until the Jamaica Accords in 1976.

archetypes-bretton-woods-gold.claim: The United States controlled two-thirds of the world's gold and insisted that Bretton Woods rest on both gold and the dollar.
archetypes-bretton-woods-gold.quote: The United States, which controlled two-thirds of the world's gold, insisted that the Bretton Woods system rest on both gold and the US dollar.

archetypes-ww2-us-two-thirds-munitions.claim: American industry produced nearly two thirds of the munitions used by Allied forces in the Second World War.
archetypes-ww2-us-two-thirds-munitions.quote: By producing nearly two thirds of the munitions used by Allied forces – including huge numbers of aircraft, ships, tanks, trucks, rifles, artillery shells, and bombs – American industry became what President Franklin D.

archetypes-ww2-crude-oil.claim: Allied crude oil output was 1,043,000,000 tonnes against 66,000,000 for the Axis.

archetypes-ww2-roosevelt-185000-aircraft.claim: In 1939 US military aircraft production was under 3,000 planes a year; Roosevelt called for 185,000 aeroplanes and 120,000 tanks in two years.
archetypes-ww2-roosevelt-185000-aircraft.quote: Roosevelt called for the production of 185,000 aeroplanes, 120,000 tanks, 55,000 anti-aircraft guns and 18 million tons of merchant shipping in two years.

archetypes-ww2-hitler-propaganda.claim: Hitler was told by his advisors that Roosevelt's target was American propaganda; in 1939 US military aircraft production was under 3,000.
archetypes-ww2-hitler-propaganda.quote: Adolf Hitler was told by his advisors that this was American propaganda; in 1939, annual aircraft production for the US military was less than 3,000 planes.

archetypes-ww2-germany-resource-dependen.claim: Germany's military production was tied to resources outside its area of control, a great disadvantage against the Allies.
archetypes-ww2-germany-resource-dependen.quote: Germany's military production was tied to resources outside its area of control, a great disadvantage as compared to the Allies.

archetypes-gaugamela-outnumbered.claim: Heavily outnumbered at Gaugamela, the Macedonian army won through superior tactics and clever use of light infantry.
archetypes-gaugamela-outnumbered.quote: Despite being heavily outnumbered, the Army of Macedon emerged victorious due to the employment of superior tactics and the clever usage of light infantry forces.

archetypes-mongol-chinese-engineers.claim: One thousand North Chinese engineer squads accompanied Hulagu Khan in his conquest of the Middle East.
archetypes-mongol-chinese-engineers.quote: One thousand North Chinese engineer squads accompanied the Mongol Hulagu Khan during his conquest of the Middle East.

archetypes-mongol-muslim-engineers-1273.claim: In 1273 the Mongols enlisted two Muslim engineers, one from Persia and one from Syria, who built counterweight trebuchets.
archetypes-mongol-muslim-engineers-1273.quote: They ultimately succeeded in reaching the city walls but in 1273, the Mongols enlisted the expertise of two Muslim engineers, one from Persia and one from Syria, who helped in the construction of counterweight trebuchets.

archetypes-mongol-unite-tribes-1206.claim: By 1206 Genghis Khan had conquered all Mongol and Turkic tribes in Mongolia and southern Siberia.
archetypes-mongol-unite-tribes-1206.quote: By 1206, Genghis Khan had conquered all Mongol and Turkic tribes in Mongolia and southern Siberia.

archetypes-lendlease-total.claim: US Lend-Lease shipped $50.1 billion of supplies, 17 per cent of US war expenditures.
archetypes-lendlease-total.quote: A total of $50.1 billion (equivalent to $709 billion in 2025 when accounting for inflation) worth of supplies was shipped, or 17 per cent of the total war expenditures of the US.

archetypes-lendlease-uk.claim: Of Lend-Lease supplies, $31.4 billion went to the United Kingdom and $11.3 billion to the Soviet Union.
archetypes-lendlease-uk.quote: In all, $31.4 billion went to the United Kingdom, $11.3 billion to the Soviet Union, $3.2 billion to France, $1.6 billion to China, and the remaining $2.6 billion to other Allies.

archetypes-ww1-german-steel-1893.claim: German steel production surpassed Britain's in 1893 and almost doubled the British effort by the outbreak of the First World War.
archetypes-ww1-german-steel-1893.quote: German steel production, the major index of industrial power, for example, surpassed that of Britain in 1893 and had almost doubled the British effort by the outbreak of the First World War.

archetypes-us-1950-share-of-activity.claim: In 1950 the United States had 6.0 percent of world population, 27.3 percent of all economic activity and 66.3 percent of world military expenditure.
archetypes-us-1950-share-of-activity.quote: Indexes of that power abound: In 1950, for instance, the United States accounted for only 6.0 percent of the world population – but 27.3 percent of all economic activity (and a far larger share of industrial production), along with 66.3 percent of world military expenditure.

archetypes-ww1-us-joined-1917.claim: The United States joined the Allies in April 1917 after Germany resumed unrestricted submarine warfare.
archetypes-ww1-us-joined-1917.quote: In April 1917, the United States joined the Allies after Germany resumed unrestricted submarine warfare against Atlantic shipping.

archetypes-ww1-schlieffen-80.claim: Under the Schlieffen Plan 80% of the German Army was on the Western Front, with the remainder screening the East.
archetypes-ww1-schlieffen-80.quote: Upon mobilisation, in accordance with the Schlieffen Plan, 80% of the German Army was located on the Western Front, with the remainder acting as a screening force in the East.

archetypes-ww2-us-enters-1941.claim: In December 1941 Japan attacked American and British territories including Pearl Harbor, leading the United States to enter the war.
archetypes-ww2-us-enters-1941.quote: In December 1941, Japan attacked American and British territories in Asia and the Pacific, including Pearl Harbor in Hawaii, leading the United States to enter the war against the Axis.

archetypes-lynx-hare-cycle.claim: The Canada lynx population rises and falls with snowshoe hare populations in a prey-predator cycle.
archetypes-lynx-hare-cycle.quote: This leads to a prey-predator cycle, as the Canada lynx population responds to the cyclic rises and falls in snowshoe hare populations over the years in Alaska and central Canada.

archetypes-napoleon-six-days-1814.claim: In the Six Days' Campaign of February 1814 the 30,000-man Grande Armée inflicted 20,000 casualties on Blucher's scattered corps at a cost of just 2,000.
archetypes-napoleon-six-days-1814.quote: In the Six Days' Campaign of February 1814, the 30,000-man Grande Armée inflicted 20,000 casualties on Field Marshal Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher's scattered corps at a cost of just 2,000 for themselves.

archetypes-ww2-coal-allies-axis.claim: Allied coal output was 4,581,400,000 tonnes against 2,629,900,000 for the Axis.

archetypes-napoleon-jena-1806.claim: The Grande Armee advanced with the bataillon-carre system and decisively defeated the Prussians at Jena and Auerstedt on 14 October 1806.
archetypes-napoleon-jena-1806.quote: The Grande Armée advanced into Prussian territory with the famed bataillon-carré (battalion square) system, whereby corps marched in close supporting distances and became vanguards, rearguards, or flank forces as the situation demanded, and decisively defeated the Prussians at Jena and Auerstedt, both fought on 14 October 1806.

archetypes-napoleon-levy-conscripts.claim: Depending on the source, the number of men conscripted by the French levy ranges from 750,000 to around 800,000.
archetypes-napoleon-levy-conscripts.quote: Depending on the source, the exact number of those conscripted ranges from 750,000 to around 800,000.

archetypes-vienna-chaumont.claim: The Treaty of Chaumont became the cornerstone of the European Alliance that formed the balance of power for decades.
archetypes-vienna-chaumont.quote: The Treaty of Chaumont became the cornerstone of the European Alliance that formed the balance of power for decades.

buildout-meta-hyperion-5gw.quote: Meta has said it will expand its Hyperion data center in Richland Parish, Louisiana, to 5 GW (gigawatts) of compute capacity from an initial 2 GW, pushing the company's planned investment in the region beyond $50 billion.

buildout-meta-elpaso-1gw.claim: Meta and BlackRock-managed funds are building a 1 GW data-centre campus in El Paso, Texas.
buildout-meta-elpaso-1gw.quote: The state-of-the-art data center campus, currently under construction in El Paso, Texas, will have 1 gigawatt of compute capacity and will play an essential role in bringing Meta's AI technologies to life, accelerating progress on AI models and supporting enhancements to the core business.

buildout-microsoft-1gw-quarter.claim: Microsoft added 31 data centres and 1 GW of capacity in the quarter to 30 June 2026.
buildout-microsoft-1gw-quarter.quote: Speaking during the company's Q4 FY2026 and full-year earnings call, CEO Satya Nadella noted that in the last quarter alone, the company added 31 data centers across five continents, contributing 1GW of capacity. – Sebastian Moss/DatacenterDynamics This follows the trend of the previous two quarters, which also saw Microsoft growing its data center capacity by 1GW each.

buildout-microsoft-2gw-fy2025.claim: Microsoft brought online 2 GW of data-centre capacity in 2025.
buildout-microsoft-2gw-fy2025.quote: In the full year of 2025, the company brought online 2GW. Nadella noted that the company remains on track to "roughly double our overall capacity in just two years." According to the company's annual report, its total footprint, including data centers, office space and other facilities, now tops 112 million sq ft (10.4m sqm).

buildout-spacex-13gw-target.claim: SemiAnalysis has SpaceX aiming for 13 GW of data-centre capacity by 2027, revised up from 10 GW.
buildout-spacex-13gw-target.quote: SemiAnalysis's latest energy model has SpaceX aiming for 13GW of data center capacity by 2027, revised up from an initial 10GW target, with roughly 3.6GW already under construction at sites it names as Colossus 2 near Memphis, a two-building complex at Starbase in Texas, and a 'TeraFab' project.

buildout-spacex-colossus2-cooling.claim: Satellite imagery in January 2026 reportedly showed Colossus 2 had cooling for 350 MW, against Musk's claim of 1 GW at launch.
buildout-spacex-colossus2-cooling.quote: Despite Musk claiming it offered 1GW of capacity at launch, satellite imagery taken in January reportedly showed it had cooling equipment installed capable of managing 350MW. In May 2026, the company was reportedly deploying 19 natural gas turbines at the site.

weapons-wework-valuation.quote: Over the following 10 years, the company raised $12.8 billion in financing at valuations as high as $47 billion

weapons-ftx-valuation.claim: As of November 2022 FTX was valued at $32 billion; it entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 11 November 2022.
weapons-ftx-valuation.quote: As of November 2022, FTX was the third-largest digital currency exchange boasting an active daily trading volume of US$10 billion and a valuation of $32 billion.

weapons-svb-failure.claim: Silicon Valley Bank failed on 10 March 2023 holding $209 billion of assets, 86.4% of its deposits uninsured: the third-largest US bank failure.
weapons-svb-failure.quote: As of the last call report of the bank, filed on December 31, 2022, it held $209 billion in total assets, with $175.5 billion in total deposits, of which the bank estimated $151.6 billion (86.4 percent) were uninsured.
